question.text: Lotus Growth Capital (Cat II PE) holds preference shares in 'Sitara Foods' with 10 lakh fully-diluted shares outstanding at an original conversion price of INR 500/share. A new Series D issue of 5 lakh shares at INR 400/share triggers BROAD-BASED weighted average anti-dilution. Adjusted conversion price (approx)?

answer.text: INR 450.00 — simple arithmetic average of INR 500 and INR 400.
INR 466.67 — broad-based WACP: OCP × (A + B) / (A + C) with A = 10 lakh fully-diluted shares, B = (5 × 400)/500 = 4 lakh deemed shares, C = 5 lakh actually issued.

explanation.text: The Logic: Broad-based weighted-average uses ALL fully-diluted shares as A. A = 10 lakh, B = (5 × 400)/500 = 2000/500 = 4 lakh deemed shares, C = 5 lakh shares actually issued. NCP = 500 × (10 + 4)/(10 + 5) = 500 × 14/15 ≈ INR 466.67. This is the standard market-practice anti-dilution adjustment. The Trap: Option A is a naive arithmetic average. Option C is full-ratchet, which over-protects the existing investor by resetting to the new round price. Option D ignores the down-round entirely. Note: The workbook (pages 227-228) supports weighted-average anti-dilution generally; this item is scoped to the broad-based variant so that the math is well-defined.
